citations.locator: section "Strawberries Frost Tolerance and Injury Symptoms"
citations.note: The source gives per-stage 30-minute, 90%-kill thresholds. The most conservative (least cold-tolerant) named flowering stage is full bloom at -1°C; earlier (tight bud, -5°C) and later (immature fruit, -2.2°C) stages tolerate more cold. -1°C is recorded as the flowering-stage damage limit because it is the stage this catalog's existing crops label 'flowering' and is the most restrictive value for that stage.
citations.quote: Strawberry flower buds and fruit are susceptible to frost injury any time after bud break (-1ºC or lower)... Strawberry flower buds can tolerate lower frost temperatures depending on its stage of development. For example tight bud flower stage can tolerate -5ºC, tight with white petals -2.2ºC, full bloom -1ºC, past full bloom and immature fruit can tolerate -2.2ºC. Note: These temperatures would have to be present for 30 minutes with an expected kill rate of 90%.
